# Ordinary spaces after aligned tab fields

`source.docx` is original, manually authored OOXML generated by
`tools/aligned_tab_tails_fixture.py`. It contains fourteen Arial controls:
right/center tab stops crossed with no tail, one/three ordinary spaces, spaces
before another tab, NBSP, spaces before a manual break, and a larger-font tail.
`native.pdf` was exported by the reference application; the reference
recorder extracts its `AB12` origins and pins the source/PDF SHA-256 hashes.
No fonts or third-party artwork are redistributed.

The reference application excludes the ordinary-space tails from right/center field alignment,
including before a subsequent tab and across formatting runs. NBSP remains
part of the alignment width. Before the fix, the three-space right field was
10.007 pt too far left and the large-font tail was 13.341 pt too far left.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.3.1.37–38 define tab stops and their paragraph settings;
§17.3.3.32 defines the inline tab. This whitespace detail is a native reference
compatibility observation, not a new serialization rule. Text, run formatting
and caret advances remain intact. Decimal-tab suffix behavior is unchanged.

The browser test compares fourteen native origins when Arial is installed and
checks editing, whitespace export, exact undo and reopening. Portable unit
tests also verify tail selection/carets, replacing a space with visible text,
mixed-size spaces and NBSP without needing a native font.
